_comment: ngsolve mhd#3 (Hartmann layers need cells proportional to 1/Ha; h_wall = L/(10*Ha) restores ~1%). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604 on the same closed-form Hartmann channel as mhd#2, at Ha = 10/30/100, comparing a cell size fixed in absolute terms against one held at the claim's L/(10*Ha). With h fixed at 0.1 the wall-shear error grows with Ha -- 1.7%, 10.5%, 42.2% -- because the layer outruns the mesh, which is what 'proportional to 1/Ha' means; with h = L/(10*Ha) the error is 0.26%, 0.24%, 0.23%, under a percent everywhere and flat in Ha, so the claim's refinement rule holds. The core velocity is accurate in all six runs. CORRECTION: the claim's '5-10x' deficit does not appear and cannot -- the computed shear is always too SMALL, never too large, so the error is one-sided and bounded by the exact value; the worst case here is a factor of 1.7. Mutation: holding the scaled runs at h = L/Ha instead of L/(10*Ha) puts them over a percent and the fixture fails on L_over_10Ha_rule_gives_under_one_percent.
